Cryptogram Solver

Find the most likely reading of a letter-substitution puzzle, using ordinary English words.

Everything runs in your browser; nothing you type is uploaded.

Answers will show up here.

Words come from the ENABLE word list, plus the one-letter words a and i. Not an official tournament word list. Offensive answers are hidden.

Up to 1,000 characters. Solving stops after 5 seconds and keeps the best answers found so far. Up to 10 answers are shown.

How to use

  1. Paste the coded sentence into "Coded text".

  2. Press "Solve". If you already know a letter, type it in "Known letters" as Q=A.

  3. Press "Show one letter" or "Show one word" for a hint, or "Copy best answer" to copy the first answer.

Example

Sam is stuck on a newspaper cryptogram and pastes the coded line, then checks Q=A.

BeforeAfter
 
YGXK LEGKT QFR LTCTF NTQKL QUG GXK YQZITKL WKGXUIZ YGKZI GF ZIOL EGFZOFTFZ Q FTV FQZOGF
FOUR SCORE AND SEVEN YEARS AGO OUR FATHERS BROUGHT FORTH ON THIS CONTINENT A NEW NATION

FAQ

Why is the first answer the one to read?

Each possible reading is scored by how common its words are. The most common reading is listed first.

What does Q=A do?

It locks the coded letter Q to the real letter A, then solves again. Write several locks separated by commas.

What if a name is not in the word list?

The solver only uses ordinary words, plus a and i. Add the letters you already know and press Solve again. Blank letters stay as underscores.

Why did an answer disappear?

Offensive answers are hidden. The line above the list says how many were hidden.

What if it is taking too long?

Solving stops after 5 seconds and shows the best answers so far. Add a known letter and press Solve again.
